title: Week in Orbit
summary: The space and defense sectors are buzzing with activity, from new contracts to strategic partnerships. Notably, the U.S. military is doubling down on satellite communications while private firms continue to jockey for position in the burgeoning space market.

themes.title: Military Contracts on the Rise
themes.body: Viasat's $307 million contract for Marine Corps satellite communications underscores a growing trend of defense spending in space. This aligns with the recent $1.4 billion increase in the FY27 budget for space resilience, indicating a robust appetite for satellite capabilities.

themes.title: Private Sector Expansion
themes.body: Rocket Lab's plans to acquire a robotics company signal a broader trend of consolidation in the space industry. Meanwhile, True Anomaly's $190 million Series C funding round highlights investor confidence in emerging space technologies.

themes.title: International Collaboration Gains Traction
themes.body: Paraguay's signing of the Artemis Accords reflects a growing international consensus on space governance. Additionally, the conclusion of the Allied space-resilience workshop in The Hague suggests that nations are increasingly prioritizing cooperative strategies in space.

themes.title: Challenges in Hypersonic Development
themes.body: The continued delays in hypersonic glide-vehicle testing raise questions about the U.S. military's pace in this critical area. As the third consecutive slip occurs, it appears that the race for hypersonic capabilities may be more complicated than anticipated.
